verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same fix: a Map from normalized email to index, built once, with appended contacts added as they arrive. Both preserve first-entry-wins and merging of duplicates within the upload. A also adds a test that pins first-entry-wins when the existing book has duplicate emails, which is the edge case an index could most easily break, and a short comment explaining the map's semantics. B leaves that behavior unprotected, which tips the decision to A.
b_issues: No test covers the first-entry-wins behavior when the existing book has duplicate emails, which is the behavior the new index could most easily regress.

verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same correct core edit: a Map from normalized email to index, with first-wins seeding and appended entries registered. This keeps the old findIndex semantics, including duplicates inside the upload. B also adds a focused test that pins the first-existing-entry-wins behavior, which is the subtle invariant the index could break, and it has a short comment explaining why. Otherwise the two are equivalent.
a_issues: No test protects the first-entry-wins behavior when the existing book already has duplicate emails, which is the main regression risk of switching to a Map.
b_issues: Single-line `if` without braces is slightly inconsistent with the surrounding style (minor).
